page.whatIsTitle: What is a Reverse Text tool?
page.whatIs:
A reverse text tool flips text in one of four ways. It can reverse every character, reverse the order of words, reverse the order of lines, or reverse the letters inside each word while keeping the words in place. Optional trim and case pattern controls let you match the formatting you need.

Character reversal walks the text by Unicode code point, which keeps emoji and non Latin scripts intact. Word reversal splits on whitespace and joins the words back in reverse order. Line reversal flips the line order while preserving each line. Letter reversal keeps word positions and whitespace, then reverses only the letters inside each word.

The case pattern option applies the original capitalisation positions to the reversed letters, so a word such as Hello becomes Olleh with the first letter still uppercase. Without that option the reversed string keeps the original character order of cases. The trim option removes leading and trailing whitespace before the operation.

The four modes mirror common string operations in programming, including the array reverse method described at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/reverse. Everything here runs locally in your browser and your text is never uploaded.
page.howToTitle: How to use Reverse Text
page.howTo:
Type or paste the text you want to transform.
Choose Reverse Characters, Reverse Word Order, Reverse Line Order or Reverse Letters.
Turn on trim whitespace when leading or trailing spaces should be removed.
Turn on preserve case when capitalisation should stay in the same positions.
Read the large preview card for a quick check of the result.
Compare the character, word and output counters.
Copy the full output with the Copy action.
page.guidanceTitle: When to use each reverse mode
page.guidance:
The preview card shows the first part of the result and names the active mode, so you can confirm at a glance that the right transformation ran. The counters show input characters, input words and output characters. A mode that only changes order keeps the character count, while trimming whitespace can reduce it. The full output block below the counters is the exact text that Copy places on your clipboard.

Reversing the characters of Hello world gives dlrow olleH, while reversing word order gives world Hello. Reversing letters in each word gives olleH dlroW when case is not preserved, and Olleh dlroW when the original case pattern is applied to the reversed letters. For a list of three lines, line reversal puts the third line first and the first line last without changing any line internally.
page.exampleInput:
Text: Hello world
Modes: Characters / Words / Lines / Letters
page.exampleOutput:
Characters: dlrow olleH
Words: world Hello
Lines: world Hello
Letters: olleH dlrow
page.exampleNote: With two words and one space, word order and line order give the same result here.
page.features:
Four reversal modes::Characters, word order, line order and letters within each word.
Unicode safe::Reversal works by code point so emoji and non Latin scripts stay whole.
Case pattern option::Capitalisation can stay in the same positions after a letter reversal.
Trim control::Leading and trailing whitespace can be removed before the transformation.
Live counters::Input characters, words and output characters update as you type.
Private operation::All transformations run locally with no uploads of your text.
page.useCases:
Playful text styling::Flip letters inside words while keeping a sentence readable.
Puzzle solving::Reverse a scrambled line or a list of clues.
Data checks::Compare input and output character counts after a transformation.
Quick formatting::Reverse a list of lines without rewriting each line manually.
page.faqs:
What is the difference between the four modes?::Character reversal flips every symbol in the string. Word reversal keeps each word intact and flips their order. Line reversal keeps each line intact and flips the line order. Letter reversal keeps words in place and flips only the letters inside each word, which is useful for stylised text.
Does the tool support emoji and other scripts?::Yes. Character and letter reversal work by Unicode code point, so emoji, accents and non Latin scripts stay intact instead of breaking into surrogate halves. Word and line reversal split on whitespace or line breaks and keep each unit unchanged.
What does preserve case do?::It maps the original capitalisation positions onto the reversed letters. A word beginning with an uppercase letter keeps an uppercase first letter after reversal. Turn it off when you want the raw reversed string with cases attached to their original characters.
What does trim whitespace remove?::It removes spaces, tabs and line breaks at the very start and end of your text before the transformation runs. Internal spacing is left alone. This is useful when pasted text has a trailing newline that would otherwise become the first character after a reversal.
Why do the counters matter?::They confirm that the transformation did what you expected. Word and line reversal keep the character count the same, while trimming can lower it. The output character count also tells you whether a long result is safe to paste into a field with a limit.
Is my text stored anywhere?::No. The transformation runs in your browser and no text is sent to a server. Only display options such as the chosen mode and switches are remembered, never the text itself.
